subject: Animation
title: Warner Bros. and Looney Tunes
description: A fast breakdown of Warner Bros. and Looney Tunes for builders.

hook.text: While Disney aimed for beauty, Warner Bros. animators aimed for laughs with chaotic energy.

buildup.text: Directors like Tex Avery and Chuck Jones created Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, and the Road Runner.

discovery.text: Warner cartoons broke the fourth wall, defied physics, and mocked Hollywood conventions openly.

twist.text: The studio paid its animators far less than Disney. The scrappy budget fueled creative rebellion.

climax.text: Looney Tunes became just as iconic as Disney, proving animation had room for irreverent comedy.

punchline.text: Low budgets and rebellion created cartoon legends.

quiz.question: How did Warner Bros. cartoons differ from Disney's approach?
options: They embraced chaotic humor, fourth-wall breaks, and irreverent comedy over beauty
They used only black and white animation
